lemma: Stately, plump Buck Mulligan
quote: Stately, plump Buck Mulligan
gloss: The iconic opening cadence of Ulysses. Based closely on Oliver St. John Gogarty (1878–1957), Dublin physician, poet, and athlete. 'Stately' parodies priestly dignity and epic gravity; 'Buck' evokes eighteenth-century Regency dandyism, hedonism, and impudent bravura.

lemma: a mirror and a razor lay crossed
quote: a mirror and a razor lay crossed
gloss: Mulligan's shaving instruments prefigure the liturgical trappings of a Catholic priest preparing for Mass. Crossed, they form the crux decussata (St. Andrew's cross) and evoke Oscar Wilde's preface to The Picture of Dorian Gray: 'The nineteenth century dislike of Realism is the rage of Caliban seeing his own face in a glass.'

lemma: Introibo ad altare Dei
quote: Introibo ad altare Dei
gloss: Latin: 'I will go in unto the altar of God.' The traditional opening versicle of the Tridentine Catholic Mass (Psalm 42:4 in the Vulgate). Spoken at the foot of the altar, Mulligan uses it here to inaugurate a mock-blessing over Dublin Bay and Sandycove from the top of the Martello Tower.
scholars: The Roman Missal (Tridentine Rite), Judica me, Deus

lemma: Chrysostomos
quote: Chrysostomos
gloss: Greek: 'Golden-mouthed' (χρυσόστομος). An epithet originally applied to Dio Chrysostom and later to St. John Chrysostom (c. 347–407 AD), Archbishop of Constantinople, celebrated for his eloquence and denunciation of clerical luxury. Stephen ironically reflects on Mulligan's gold-capped teeth and caustic, irreverent tongue.

lemma: the gunrest
quote: the gunrest
gloss: The circular granite firing platform atop the Sandycove Martello Tower (Tower No. 11, built 1804 by the British Board of Ordnance). It served as an emplacement for a rotating 24-pounder cannon facing out across Dublin Bay. In 1904, Gogarty leased it from the War Office for £8 a year.

lemma: The snotgreen sea. The scrotumtightening sea.
quote: The snotgreen sea. The scrotumtightening sea.
gloss: Mulligan's notorious compound epithets. Parodies classical Homeric formulas ('wine-dark sea', epi oinopa ponton) through visceral bodily realism and mock-medical vernacular. Also alludes to the emerald green flag of Irish nationalism and the Greek sea god Proteus.

lemma: The rage of Caliban at not seeing his face in a glass
quote: The rage of Caliban at not seeing his face in a glass
gloss: Direct quotation from Oscar Wilde's preface to The Picture of Dorian Gray (1891): 'The nineteenth century dislike of Romanticism is the rage of Caliban not seeing his own face in a glass.' Caliban represents the savage, colonized subject in Shakespeare's The Tempest; here Mulligan casts Stephen as the resentful, melancholic poet gazing into the cracked lookingglass of Ireland.

lemma: cracked lookingglass of a servant
quote: cracked lookingglass of a servant
gloss: Stephen's stinging definition of Irish art under British and Vatican colonial subjugation. Synthesizes Wilde's aphorism with Swift's Preface to The Battle of the Books ('Satyr is a sort of Glass, wherein Beholders do generally discover every body's Face but their Own'). Establishes the domestic servant status of Ireland.

lemma: Liliata rutilantium te confessorum
quote: Liliata rutilantium te confessorum
gloss: Latin hymn from the Ordo Commendationis Animae (the Catholic Roman Ritual for the Commendation of a Departing Soul): 'May the glittering throng of confessors, white as lilies, encompass thee.' Stephen prayed this at the deathbed of his mother May Dedalus (née Mary Joyce), an agony that haunts him throughout the entire day of June 16, 1904.

lemma: Agenbite of inwit
quote: Agenbite of inwit
gloss: Middle English phrase: 'Again-bite of inner wit' (the remorse of conscience), from Dan Michel of Northgate's 1340 Kentish translation of Ayenbite of Inwyt (itself a translation of Friar Lorens' Somme le Roi). Serves as Stephen Dedalus's primary recurrent guilt motif over his refusal to kneel and pray at his dying mother's bedside.

lemma: the usurper
quote: the usurper
gloss: Stephen's silent, bitter epithet for Buck Mulligan at the conclusion of Episode 1. Directly links the episode to Homer's Odyssey, where Antinous and the insolent suitors usurp Telemachus's patrimony and feast in Odysseus's hall. Mulligan has taken Stephen's key and money, leaving Stephen dispossessed.

lemma: — You, Cochrane, what city sent for him?
quote: — You, Cochrane, what city sent for him?
gloss: Opening line of Episode 2 (Nestor). Stephen Dedalus is teaching an ancient history lesson on Pyrrhus of Epirus at the Clifton School in Dalkey. The classroom setting establishes the episode's art (History) and catechistic technique.

lemma: Another victory like that and we are done for.
quote: Another victory like that and we are done for.
gloss: The classic definition of a Pyrrhic victory after the Battle of Asculum (279 BC). Stephen reflects on the futility of military triumphs, foreshadowing his upcoming discussion on the nightmare of history with the headmaster Mr. Deasy.

lemma: Ineluctable modality of the visible
quote: Ineluctable modality of the visible
gloss: The famous philosophical opening of Episode 3 (Proteus). Stephen walks along Sandymount Strand meditating on Aristotle's De Anima and Sense and Sensibilia: that visual perception is constrained by light and color ('the diaphane').

lemma: Signatures of all things I am here to read
quote: Signatures of all things I am here to read
gloss: Allusion to German mystic Jacob Boehme's De Signatura Rerum (The Signature of All Things, 1621). The external natural world (seaspawn, seawrack, rusty boots) presents divine glyphs requiring hermeneutic interpretation.

lemma: Mr Leopold Bloom ate with relish the inner organs of beasts and fowls.
quote: Mr Leopold Bloom ate with relish the inner organs of beasts and fowls.
gloss: The iconic opening sentence of Part II (The Odyssey) and Episode 4 (Calypso), introducing Leopold Bloom at 8:00 AM in the kitchen of 7 Eccles Street. Immediately establishes Bloom's earthy, visceral, and sensuous humanity in contrast to Stephen Dedalus's scholastic asceticism.

lemma: grilled mutton kidneys which gave to his palate a fine tang of faintly scented urine
quote: grilled mutton kidneys which gave to his palate a fine tang of faintly scented urine
gloss: Key anatomical correspondence for Calypso: the Kidney (organ). Joyce foregrounds somatic biology and gastrointestinal reality, evoking Homer's epic feasts through the modest breakfast of a Dublin advertising canvasser.

lemma: By lorries along sir John Rogerson's quay Mr Bloom walked soberly
quote: By lorries along sir John Rogerson's quay Mr Bloom walked soberly
gloss: Opening of Episode 5 (Lotus Eaters). 10:00 AM. Leopold Bloom walks through the south docklands towards Westland Row, enveloped in the heavy atmosphere of narcotic ease, botanical languor, and colonial inertia corresponding to Homer's land of the Lotus-eaters.

lemma: Henry Flower
quote: Henry Flower
gloss: Bloom's undercover epistolary pseudonym for his secret romantic correspondence with Martha Clifford. The flower motif reinforces the botanical and narcotic themes of the episode.

lemma: Martin Cunningham, first, pushed homely yellow chipped stone
quote: Martin Cunningham, first, pushed homely yellow chipped stone
gloss: Opening of Episode 6 (Hades). 11:00 AM. Leopold Bloom boards the funeral carriage at Sandymount for Paddy Dignam's burial at Prospect Cemetery in Glasnevin. The journey through Dublin represents Odysseus's nekyia (descent into the Underworld).

lemma: Martin Cunningham's face was like a block of carved limestone.
quote: Martin Cunningham's face was like a block of carved limestone.
gloss: Martin Cunningham represents Sisyphus in the Homeric scheme. His face resembles the limestone rock of Dublin, burdened by his tragic family life (an alcoholic wife), yet maintaining gentle Christian compassion.

lemma: IN THE HEART OF THE HIBERNIAN METROPOLIS
quote: IN THE HEART OF THE HIBERNIAN METROPOLIS
gloss: The celebrated opening headline of Episode 7 (Aeolus). 12:00 PM (Noon). Set in the newspaper offices of The Freeman's Journal and Evening Telegraph. Joyce introduces 63 newspaper headlines that mock imperial rhetoric, journalistic sensationalism, and the gusty winds of Dublin political speech.

lemma: Nelson's pillar
quote: Nelson's pillar
gloss: Nelson's Pillar in O'Connell Street (then Sackville Street), the central tramway hub of Dublin. The monument to the British naval hero Horatio Nelson symbolizes imperial dominance over Dublin, later mocked in Stephen Dedalus's 'Parable of the Plums'.

lemma: Pineapple rock, lemon platt, butter scotch.
quote: Pineapple rock, lemon platt, butter scotch.
gloss: Opening cadence of Episode 8 (Lestrygonians). 1:00 PM. Leopold Bloom gazes into the confectioner's window of Graham Lemon on Sackville Street. The episode's organ is the Esophagus and its technique is Peristalsis, saturating the narrative with hunger, chewing, digestion, and predatory consumerism.

lemma: Elijah is coming.
quote: Elijah is coming.
gloss: An evangelical throwaway flyer advertising the apocalyptic revival meetings of Dr. John Alexander Dowie. Bloom receives it and later casts it upon the River Liffey, where it bobs downstream towards Dublin Bay throughout the afternoon.

lemma: Urbane, to comfort them, the quaker librarian purred:
quote: Urbane, to comfort them, the quaker librarian purred:
gloss: Opening of Episode 9 (Scylla and Charybdis). 2:00 PM. Set in the National Library of Ireland on Kildare Street. Introduces Thomas William Lyster, the scholarly quaker librarian, engaging with George Russell (A.E.), John Eglinton, and Stephen Dedalus as Stephen prepares his dialectical Hamlet theory.

lemma: Shakespeare's grandson is Shakespeare's grandfather
quote: Shakespeare's grandson is Shakespeare's grandfather
gloss: Stephen's celebrated theological-literary paradox: applying the Sabellian heresy and Trinitarian dogma to Shakespeare's ghost in Hamlet, arguing that the artist is the father of all his creations and his own spiritual progenitor.

lemma: The superior, the very reverend John Conmee S.J. reset his smooth watch in his pocket
quote: The superior, the very reverend John Conmee S.J. reset his smooth watch in his pocket
gloss: Opening of Episode 10 (Wandering Rocks). 3:00 PM. Father John Conmee, S.J., former rector of Clongowes Wood College, begins his afternoon walk through the north side of Dublin. The episode is structured in 19 synchronous mini-scenes weaving across the civic labyrinth of Dublin.

lemma: Clongowes Wood College
quote: Clongowes Wood College
gloss: Joyce's Jesuit boarding school in County Kildare, prominently featured in A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man. Conmee represents the spiritual authority of Rome in Ireland alongside the Viceroy's British imperial power.

lemma: Bronze by gold heard the hoofirons, steelyringing.
quote: Bronze by gold heard the hoofirons, steelyringing.
gloss: The famous polyphonic opening chord of Episode 11 (Sirens). 4:00 PM. Set in the Ormond Hotel bar on the Liffey quays. 'Bronze' represents the bronze-haired barmaid Lydia Douce; 'gold' represents Mina Kennedy. The first sixty lines form a musical overture announcing all acoustic themes developed across the episode.

lemma: Imperthnthn thnthnthn.
quote: Imperthnthn thnthnthn.
gloss: Acoustic deformation of 'impertinent insolence', mimicking the rhythm and dissonance of musical notes sounding together in a fugue ('fuga per canonem').

lemma: I was just passing the time of day with old Troy of the D.M.P.
quote: I was just passing the time of day with old Troy of the D.M.P.
gloss: Opening of Episode 12 (Cyclops). 5:00 PM. Barney Kiernan's pub on Little Britain Street. Narrated by an unnamed Dublin debt-collector using cynical, vernacular Dublin slang, juxtaposed against 33 hyperbolic parodies written in heroic, Ossianic, legal, and biblical styles ('gigantism').

lemma: The citizen
quote: The citizen
gloss: Modeled closely on Michael Cusack (1847–1906), founder of the Gaelic Athletic Association (GAA). The Citizen embodies militant, narrow, and anti-Semitic Irish chauvinism, acting as the one-eyed Cyclops (Polyphemus) who hurls a biscuit-tin at Bloom.

lemma: The summer evening had begun to fold the world in its mysterious embrace.
quote: The summer evening had begun to fold the world in its mysterious embrace.
gloss: Opening cadence of Episode 13 (Nausicaa). 8:00 PM. Sandymount Strand. Joyce adopts the sentimental, cliché-ridden prose of Victorian romantic magazines (The Lady's Pictorial) to narrate the inner fantasy world of Gerty MacDowell, who sits on the strand gazing across at Leopold Bloom.

lemma: Gerty MacDowell
quote: Gerty MacDowell
gloss: Gerty represents Homer's Phaeacian princess Nausicaa, who discovers the shipwrecked Odysseus on the shore. Joyce pairs her youth and physical disability (a subtle limp) with the litany of the Virgin Mary sounding from the nearby Star of the Sea church.

lemma: Deshil Holles Eamus. Deshil Holles Eamus. Deshil Holles Eamus.
quote: Deshil Holles Eamus. Deshil Holles Eamus. Deshil Holles Eamus.
gloss: The incantatory opening of Episode 14 (Oxen of the Sun). 10:00 PM. Holles Street National Maternity Hospital. Fuses Irish 'deiseal' (sunwise, auspicious direction), Holles Street, and Latin 'eamus' ('Let us go sunwise to Holles Street'). Joyce constructs the episode as an exact chronological evolution of English prose style (from Latinate incantations and Old English alliteration to Carlyle and modern slang), mimicking the nine-month gestation of a human fetus.

lemma: Send us bright one, light one, Horhorn, quickening and wombfruit.
quote: Send us bright one, light one, Horhorn, quickening and wombfruit.
gloss: Invocation mimicking early medieval Anglo-Saxon alliterative verse. The organ is the Womb and the art is Medicine, tracking Mina Purefoy's protracted labor within the hospital while Stephen and medical students drink beer in the common room.

lemma: THE MABBOT STREET ENTRANCE
quote: THE MABBOT STREET ENTRANCE
gloss: Opening stage direction of Episode 15 (Circe). 12:00 AM (Midnight). Dublin's red-light district (Nighttown / Monto), centered around Tyrone and Mabbot Streets. Structured entirely as an expressionist theatrical playscript where psychological repressions, hallucinations, and guilt figures materialize physically.

lemma: Nighttown
quote: Nighttown
gloss: Joyce's term for the Monto brothel quarter of Dublin, at the time the largest red-light district in the British Isles. Corresponds to Circe's island of Aeaea where men are transformed into swine.

lemma: Preparatory to anything else Mr Bloom brushed off the dust from Stephen's clothes.
quote: Preparatory to anything else Mr Bloom brushed off the dust from Stephen's clothes.
gloss: Opening of Part III (The Nostos) and Episode 16 (Eumaeus). 1:00 AM. Leopold Bloom guides an exhausted, shaken Stephen Dedalus to the cabman's shelter under Loopline Bridge near Custom House Quay. Written in an intentionally fatigued, cliché-laden, and circumlocutory prose style reflecting somatic physical exhaustion.

lemma: Skin-the-Goat
quote: Skin-the-Goat
gloss: James Fitzharris (1833–1910), nicknamed 'Skin-the-Goat', driver of the getaway cab in the 1882 Phoenix Park Murders of Lord Frederick Cavendish and Thomas Henry Burke. He runs the cabman's shelter, embodying unrepentant Fenian physical force nationalism.

lemma: What parallel courses did Bloom and Stephen follow returning?
quote: What parallel courses did Bloom and Stephen follow returning?
gloss: The famous opening question of Episode 17 (Ithaca). 2:00 AM. 7 Eccles Street. Joyce's favorite episode, composed entirely in impersonal, scientific catechism (questions and answers). Reduces the heroic homecoming of Odysseus and Telemachus to mathematical equations, astronomical coordinates, and physical laws.

lemma: the key of the front door was in the pocket of the other trousers
quote: the key of the front door was in the pocket of the other trousers
gloss: The comedic climax of the homecoming: Bloom has forgotten the latchkey of 7 Eccles Street in his morning trousers, mirroring Stephen's earlier dispossession of the Martello Tower key by Buck Mulligan in Episode 1.

lemma: Yes because he never did a thing like that before as ask to get his breakfast in bed
quote: Yes because he never did a thing like that before as ask to get his breakfast in bed
gloss: The triumphant opening phrase of Episode 18 (Penelope). The unpunctuated stream-of-consciousness monologue of Molly Bloom lying in bed at 7 Eccles Street beside her sleeping husband. Composed of eight unpunctuated giant paragraphs, beginning with the primordial affirmation 'Yes' and ending with the ecstatic embrace on Howth Head.

lemma: Howth
quote: Howth
gloss: Howth Head, the dramatic promontory overlooking Dublin Bay where Leopold proposed to Molly among the rhododendrons sixteen years earlier in 1888. The geography anchors both Ulysses and Finnegans Wake (Howth Castle and Environs).
